extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and practitioners before the USPTO (especially trademark practitioners representing foreign-domiciled applicants) and persons subject to OED discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing practitioner conduct before the USPTO in trademark matters (including the U.S. Counsel Rule, duties of competence, diligence, communication, signature control, non-practitioner supervision), and the remedial/monitoring obligations imposed as conditions of reinstatement after discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. Counsel Rule (representation of foreign-domiciled applicants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective August 3, 2019, trademark applicants not domiciled within the United States must be represented by an attorney who is licensed to practice law in a jurisdiction of the United States (the "U.S. Counsel Rule").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners representing foreign-domiciled trademark applicants must ensure they are the authorized U.S.-licensed attorney of record and comply with all obligations attendant to that representation (e.g., sufficient review of filings, certification duties).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to review and certify truthfulness (37 C.F.R. § 11.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.18, a practitioner is required to review sufficiently clients' applications in order to certify that he believes all statements made therein to be true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review must include inquiries reasonable under the circumstances (e.g., verifying specimens show marks as used in commerce and that specimens are authentic, not mockups or digitally altered) before presenting documents to the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent representation (37 C.F.R. § 11.101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall provide competent representation to a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competence violations include accepting a volume of clients so large that the practitioner cannot conduct adequate review of trademark filings prior to filing; failing to review applications that agents signed and filed where practitioner is attorney of record; and failing to implement procedures to ensure compliance with USPTO regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable diligence and promptness (37 C.F.R. § 11.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations include not conducting sufficiently thorough reviews prior to filing, failing to implement procedures to ensure filings comply with USPTO regulations, failing to ensure adequate communication of USPTO-issued correspondence with clients, and failing to act on Office Actions unless a draft response is provided by an agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable consultation about means to accomplish objectives (37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall reasonably consult with the client about the means by which the client's objectives are to be accomplished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to ensure that applicant decisions regarding important USPTO-issued correspondence were communicated to the practitioner (e.g., relying on agents without confirmation) breaches this duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep clients reasonably informed (37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall keep clients reasonably informed about the status of a matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes ensuring clients receive and are informed of Office Actions and other important USPTO correspondence; practitioners must not interpret agent silence as client authorization to abandon response without confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain matters sufficiently for informed decisions (37 C.F.R. § 11.104(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall explain matters to the extent reasonably necessary to permit clients to make informed decisions regarding the representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must timely inform clients about material events (e.g., impermissible signings and potential adverse consequences to IP rights) so clients can decide how to proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not knowingly making false statements / correct false statements (37 C.F.R. § 11.303(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall not knowingly make a false statement of fact to a tribunal or fail to correct in a timely manner a false statement of material fact made to the tribunal by the practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of violations: allowing another person to enter practitioner's signature on applications and failing to inform the USPTO; submitting declarations without conducting a reasonable inquiry into veracity of the averments; failing to promptly notify the USPTO upon learning of falsity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable efforts to ensure non-practitioners' conduct is compatible (37 C.F.R. § 11.503(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall make reasonable efforts to ensure that the conduct of non-practitioner assistants is compatible with the professional obligations of the practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations include allowing non-practitioners to prepare and file trademark documents without proper review and vetting, failing to ensure adequate communication of USPTO correspondence, and authorizing non-practitioners to enter practitioner's signature on filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not assisting unauthorized practice of law (37 C.F.R. § 11.505)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall not assist another in practicing law in a jurisdiction in violation of that jurisdiction's regulation of the legal profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes allowing non-practitioners to prepare and file trademark filings on behalf of clients that practitioner had not reviewed, and authorizing non-practitioners to prepare and enter practitioner's signature on filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding conduct involving dishonesty (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall not engage in conduct involving dishonesty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: signing declarations that specimens show marks as used in commerce without performing a reasonable inquiry; authorizing non-practitioners to enter practitioner's signature and failing to inform the USPTO of improper filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding conduct prejudicial to administration of justice (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall not engage in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: failing to review specimens for authenticity (e.g., mockups or digitally altered images), not conducting a reasonable inquiry under § 11.18 before presenting documents to the USPTO that the Office will rely upon in examination and issuance of registrations, and permitting unauthorized signatures on filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature control and prohibition on unauthorized signing
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must not authorize non-practitioners or others to enter the practitioner's signature on trademark applications or declarations and must report impermissible signings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an impermissible signing occurs, practitioner must timely inform clients and the USPTO; failure to do so is cited as misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to prepare plan for reasonable inquiry into specimens and use-in-commerce
rubrics_metrics.description: As a condition of reinstatement, practitioner must consult a U.S.-licensed attorney (≥5 years federal trademark experience) and prepare a detailed plan outlining intended future practice for making a reasonable inquiry that specimens are authentic and that identified goods/services are being used in commerce at key filing/maintenance stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan must address inquiries at §1(a) filing, Statement of Use for §1(b) applications, §8 Declarations (five-year continuous use), and subsequent renewals; plan must be presented to OED Director as part of any petition for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to prepare plan for handling Office Actions
rubrics_metrics.description: As a condition of reinstatement, practitioner must consult a U.S.-licensed attorney and prepare a detailed plan for handling Office Actions, including learning that Office Actions have been issued, informing clients (directly or via bona-fide intermediaries), receiving and memorializing confirmation that clients were informed, receiving and memorializing client instructions regarding Office Actions, and memorializing instructions not to respond (abandonment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan must be presented to the OED Director as part of any petition for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to prepare plan for conflicts checking
rubrics_metrics.description: As a condition of reinstatement, practitioner must consult a U.S.-licensed attorney and prepare a detailed plan outlining intended future practice for conflicts-of-interest checking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan must be presented to OED Director as part of any petition for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice management plan to ensure thorough review (U.S. Counsel Rule and §11.18 compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of reinstatement, practitioner must prepare and present a plan outlining intended future practice for ensuring trademark applications are thoroughly reviewed consistent with the U.S. Counsel Rule and § 11.18 (e.g., plans for increasing non-practitioner staff, reducing number of trademark application clients).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan is to be presented to the OED Director with any petition for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing legal education (CLE) requirements for reinstatement and probation
rubrics_metrics.description: As a condition of reinstatement and during probation the practitioner must complete specified CLE credits: (1) a sworn affidavit showing completion of two (2) hours of CLE on law office management as condition of reinstatement; (2) within first 12 months of probationary period, a sworn affidavit showing completion of six (6) hours of CLE on trademark practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence of CLE must be provided to the OED Director as part of reinstatement/probation compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probationary monitoring: TESS searches and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: During an 18-month probationary period after reinstatement, practitioner must on at least a biweekly basis search TESS for applications identifying him as attorney of record and promptly inform USPTO personnel in writing of any filings identifying him as attorney of record that were not made by him or with his knowledge and consent; and on a quarterly basis submit a written report to the OED Director stating completion of the searches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This monitoring is a condition of probation and failure to comply may trigger Orders to Show Cause and further suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation with USPTO investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall cooperate fully with the USPTO in any present or future USPTO inquiry made into improper filings of trademark documents by entities with whom the practitioner works or has worked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cooperation is reflected in mitigation and is an ongoing obligation under the settlement terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on USPTO.gov account access and use
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective after limited winding-up period, USPTO.gov accounts under practitioner's control shall be terminated/suspended/deactivated and practitioner is prohibited from using, accessing, opening, applying for, verifying credentials for, or sponsoring any USPTO.gov account(s) to be used for filing trademark documents until reinstatement is granted; limited recognition for 30 days for winding up and narrow supervised paralegal access under §11.58(h) are exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioner must inform OED of any accounts he opened and must authorize USPTO to suspend/deactivate such accounts; USPTO may take actions to prevent account creation or activation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to access certain Fee Processing Next Generation System accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Final Order prevents the practitioner from having access to Fee Processing Next Generation System accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a narrowly preserved access right despite broader prohibitions on trademark filing system accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Client notification requirements during suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner may satisfy obligations to provide written notice of the order of suspension to foreign-domiciled clients by emailing a copy of the Final Order correctly translated into the client's native language to the email address provided in the 'Applicant's Information' portion of the client's trademark application or to another email address known to belong to the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an approved method to notify foreign clients of suspension under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(c)(3)(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public notice of disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order in OED's FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the specified Notice of Suspension and Probation text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication includes the factual summary of misconduct, the rules violated, and the sanctions imposed; such publication may be considered in future disciplinary proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of rights and procedural consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: By agreement, the practitioner may waive rights to seek reconsideration, review, or appeal of the Final Order; the OED Director will file a motion dismissing pending disciplinary action without prejudice after entry of a Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver affects post-order remedies and procedural posture; failure to comply with probationary conditions may prompt Orders to Show Cause and additional suspension up to nine months.
